results.title: Growth function of a generating family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P$ be a generating family of a group $G$. The growth function $\gamma_P$ of $P$ assigns to each natural number $n$ the number of elements $g \in G$ whose word length with respect to $P$ is at most $n$, that is, the cardinality of the ball of radius $n$ in the word metric of $P$; when this ball is infinite, $\gamma_P(n)$ is taken to be $0$.

results.title: Polynomial growth
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P$ be a generating family of a group $G$, with growth function $\gamma_P$. Then $P$ has polynomial growth if, for every natural number $n$, the ball of radius $n$ (the set of elements of $G$ of word length at most $n$ with respect to $P$) is finite, and there are natural numbers $C$ and $d$ such that $\gamma_P(n) \le C (n + 1)^d$ for every natural number $n$.

results.title: The growth function at radius zero
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: For every generating family $P$ of a group $G$, the growth function of $P$ takes the value $1$ at $0$: the ball of radius $0$ consists of the identity element alone.

results.title: The growth function of a finite group is positive
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: For every generating family $P$ of a finite group $G$ and every natural number $n$, the growth function of $P$ is positive at $n$: the ball of radius $n$ contains the identity.

results.title: The growth function is bounded by the order of the group
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: For every generating family $P$ of a finite group $G$ and every natural number $n$, the value of the growth function of $P$ at $n$ is at most the order of $G$, since every ball is a subset of $G$.

results.title: Finite groups have polynomial growth
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every generating family of a finite group has polynomial growth: its growth function is bounded by the order of the group, a polynomial of degree $0$.

results.title: Polynomial growth makes the growth function positive
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: If a generating family $P$ of a group $G$ has polynomial growth, then the growth function of $P$ is positive at every natural number $n$.

results.title: Augmentation ideal of the integral group ring
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a group $G$, the augmentation ideal $\Delta(G)$ of the integral group ring $\mathbb{Z}G$ is the $\mathbb{Z}$-submodule spanned by the elements $g - 1$ for $g \in G$. It is the kernel of the augmentation map $\mathbb{Z}G \to \mathbb{Z}$, $\sum_g a_g g \mapsto \sum_g a_g$.

results.title: Dimension subgroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\Delta(G)$ be the augmentation ideal of the integral group ring $\mathbb{Z}G$ of a group $G$, and for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\Delta(G)^n$ be its $n$-th power, the $\mathbb{Z}$-span of all products of $n$ elements of $\Delta(G)$. An element $g \in G$ lies in the $n$-th dimension subgroup $D_n(G) = G \cap (1 + \Delta(G)^n)$ when $g - 1 \in \Delta(G)^n$.

results.title: Gupta–Kuz'min centrality question (Kourovka 12.22(a))
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every group $G$, every $n \ge 1$, every element $x$ of the $n$-th dimension subgroup $D_n(G)$ and every $g \in G$, the commutator $x g x^{-1} g^{-1}$ lies in $\gamma_n(G)$, the $n$-th term of the lower central series of $G$, indexed so that $\gamma_1(G) = G$ and $\gamma_{k+1}(G) = [\gamma_k(G), G]$. Equivalently, the image of $D_n(G)$ in $G/\gamma_n(G)$ is central.

results.title: Gupta–Kuz'min exponent question (Kourovka 12.22(b))
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every group $G$, every $n \ge 1$ and every element $x$ of the $n$-th dimension subgroup $D_n(G)$, the square $x^2$ lies in $\gamma_n(G)$, the $n$-th term of the lower central series of $G$, indexed so that $\gamma_1(G) = G$ and $\gamma_{k+1}(G) = [\gamma_k(G), G]$. Equivalently, the image of $D_n(G)$ in $G/\gamma_n(G)$ has exponent dividing $2$.

results.title: Dimension quotients need not be central
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a group $G$, an integer $n \ge 1$, an element $x$ of the $n$-th dimension subgroup $D_n(G)$ and an element $g \in G$ such that the commutator $x g x^{-1} g^{-1}$ does not lie in $\gamma_n(G)$, the $n$-th term of the lower central series of $G$ (indexed so that $\gamma_1(G) = G$). That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 12.22(a) is negative: the image of $D_n(G)$ in $G/\gamma_n(G)$ need not be central.

results.title: Dimension quotients need not have exponent dividing 2
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a group $G$, an integer $n \ge 1$ and an element $x$ of the $n$-th dimension subgroup $D_n(G)$ such that $x^2$ does not lie in $\gamma_n(G)$, the $n$-th term of the lower central series of $G$ (indexed so that $\gamma_1(G) = G$). That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 12.22(b) is negative: the image of $D_n(G)$ in $G/\gamma_n(G)$ need not have exponent dividing $2$.

results.title: Digit reversal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $b$ and $n$ with $b \ge 2$, write $n = \sum_{i\lt k} d_i b^i$ with digits $0 \le d_i < b$ and leading digit $d_{k-1} \ne 0$ (so $k = 0$ when $n = 0$). results.title: Two floor-function identities
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $x$, the sum $\lfloor x \rfloor + \lfloor -x \rfloor$ equals $0$ if $x$ is an integer and $-1$ otherwise. For all real numbers $x$ and $y$, $\lfloor x + y \rfloor = \lfloor x \rfloor + \lfloor y \rfloor$ if $(x - \lfloor x \rfloor) + (y - \lfloor y \rfloor) < 1$, and $\lfloor x + y \rfloor = \lfloor x \rfloor + \lfloor y \rfloor + 1$ otherwise.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ be a sequence in a normed additive commutative group $\alpha$. If $\|f(n)\|^{1/n}$ tends to a real limit $l$ with $l < 1$ as $n \to \infty$, then the series $\sum_n \|f(n)\|$ converges.

results.title: Cauchy's root test, convergence case
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ be a sequence in a complete normed additive commutative group $\alpha$. If $\|f(n)\|^{1/n}$ tends to a real limit $l$ with $l < 1$ as $n \to \infty$, then $f$ is summable, that is, the series $\sum_n f(n)$ converges unconditionally.

results.title: Cauchy's root test, divergence case

results.title: Rectangle uniqueness for measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ be finite measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$. If $\mu_1((a, b]) = \mu_2((a, b])$ for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $a_i \le b_i$ for every $i$, where $(a, b] = \prod_{i=1}^d (a_i, b_i]$, then $\mu_1 = \mu_2$.

results.title: Uniqueness from rectangle values
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$, and let $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ be measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Suppose that for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $a_i \le b_i$ for every $i$, both $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ assign the rectangle $(a, b] = \prod_{i=1}^d (a_i, b_i]$ the mass $\max(\Delta_{a,b} F, 0)$, where $\Delta_{a,b} F$ is the rectangle value of $F$ at $a, b$. Then $\mu_1 = \mu_2$.

results.summary: The statement that for every real $C > 0$ there is a real constant $K$ such that $r_3(N) \le K N / (\log N)^C$ for every natural number $N \ge 2$, where $r_3(N)$ is the largest size of a subset of $\{0, 1, \dots, N - 1\}$ containing no non-trivial three-term arithmetic progression.

results.title: Finite antichain covers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a partially ordered set. A finite family $C$ of finite subsets of $\alpha$ is a finite antichain cover of $\alpha$ when every member of $C$ is an antichain and every element of $\alpha$ belongs to some member of $C$.

results.title: Maximum chain size
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite partially ordered set $\alpha$, the maximum chain size of $\alpha$ is the largest cardinality of a chain in $\alpha$, that is, of a set of pairwise comparable elements.

results.title: Minimum antichain cover size
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite partially ordered set $\alpha$, the minimum antichain cover size of $\alpha$ is the smallest number of antichains in $\alpha$ whose union is all of $\alpha$.

results.title: Dual of Dilworth's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite partially ordered set $\alpha$, the maximum chain size of $\alpha$ equals its minimum antichain cover size: the largest cardinality of a chain in $\alpha$ equals the smallest number of antichains whose union is $\alpha$.

results.title: Mirsky's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite partially ordered set $\alpha$, the maximum chain size of $\alpha$ equals its minimum antichain cover size: the largest cardinality of a chain in $\alpha$ equals the smallest number of antichains whose union is $\alpha$.

results.title: Poset matrix

results.title: Relation represented by a Boolean matrix

results.title: Diagonal entries of a poset matrix

results.title: Transitivity of the true entries of a poset matrix

results.title: The relation of a poset matrix is reflexive

results.title: The relation of a poset matrix is transitive

results.title: Simplex vertices
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a vertex type $V$. A simplex vertex of $G$ is a finite set $s$ of vertices that is a clique of $G$, meaning that any two distinct elements of $s$ are adjacent in $G$.

results.title: Empty simplex vertex
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph. The empty simplex vertex of $G$ is the empty set of vertices, which is a clique of $G$.

results.title: Singleton simplex vertex
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph. For a vertex $v$ of $G$, the singleton simplex vertex of $v$ is the one-element set containing $v$, which is a clique of $G$.

results.title: Simplex graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph. The simplex graph of $G$ is the simple graph whose vertices are the simplex vertices of $G$ (the finite cliques of $G$), in which two cliques $s$ and $t$ are adjacent exactly when their symmetric difference $s \triangle t$ has exactly one element.

results.title: Adjacency in the simplex graph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph. Two simplex vertices $s$ and $t$ of $G$ are adjacent in the simplex graph of $G$ if and only if their symmetric difference $s \triangle t$ has exactly one element.

results.title: The empty clique is adjacent to every singleton
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph. For every vertex $v$ of $G$, the empty simplex vertex of $G$ and the singleton simplex vertex of $v$ are adjacent in the simplex graph of $G$.

results.title: Minimum test set instance
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of MINIMUM TEST SET is a triple $(n, C, K)$ of a natural number $n$ (the number of elements), a finite list $C$ of finite lists of natural numbers (the tests) and a natural number $K$ (the bound).

results.title: Well-formed minimum test set instance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, C, K)$ of MINIMUM TEST SET is well formed when every test in the list $C$ is a list of numbers below $n$ without repeated entries, so that each test lists a subset of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, each element once.

results.title: Feasible minimum test set instance

results.title: Raw input edge
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A raw edge is an undirected weighted input edge given by three natural numbers: two endpoints, which are not yet checked to be vertices of the graph, and a weight.

results.title: Kruskal input graph
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, an input graph on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ consists of a list of raw edges, kept in input order; the same pair of endpoints may occur on several edges.

results.title: Weighted edge
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A weighted edge on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ consists of an ordinal, a natural number recording its zero-based position in the original input list, two endpoints in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and a natural-number weight.

results.title: Sorting key of a weighted edge
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The sorting key of a weighted edge $e$ is the pair $(w(e), i(e)) \in \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ of its weight $w(e)$ and its input ordinal $i(e)$, the zero-based position of $e$ in the original input edge list.

results.title: Lexicographic order on edge keys
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For pairs of natural numbers $(w, i)$ and $(w', i')$, $(w, i) \preceq (w', i')$ holds when $w < w'$, or $w = w'$ and $i \le i'$. This is the non-strict lexicographic order on $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$; Kruskal's algorithm applies it to keys (weight, input ordinal).

results.title: Decoding a raw edge at an ordinal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given natural numbers $n$ and $i$ and a raw edge with source $s$, target $t$ and weight $w$, decoding at ordinal $i$ returns the validated edge on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with ordinal $i$, source $s$, target $t$ and weight $w$ when $s < n$ and $t < n$, and returns no edge otherwise.

results.title: Validating an edge list from a given ordinal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given $n$, a starting ordinal $o$ and a list of raw edges $e_0, e_1, \dots, e_{m-1}$, this returns, in input order, the weighted edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ obtained from those $e_k$ whose two endpoints are both less than $n$; each keeps the endpoints and weight of $e_k$ and carries the ordinal $o + k$. Edges with an endpoint at least $n$ are omitted, but they still count towards the ordinals of later…

results.title: Valid edges of an input graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a graph $G$ on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ given by its list of raw edges $e_0, e_1, \dots, e_{m-1}$, the valid edges of $G$ are, in input order, the weighted edges obtained from those $e_k$ whose two endpoints are both less than $n$; each keeps the endpoints and weight of $e_k$ and carries its zero-based input ordinal $k$. Edges with an endpoint at least $n$ are omitted.

results.title: Sorting edges by weight and input position
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Sorting a list of validated edges is merge sort with the comparison $(w, i) \preceq (w', i')$ if $w < w'$, or $w = w'$ and $i \le i'$, applied to the pairs (weight, input position) of the edges.

results.title: Valid edges in Kruskal order
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite weighted multigraph $G$ on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the ordered edges of $G$ are its valid input edges (those whose endpoints are both less than $n$), sorted by merge sort in lexicographic order of (weight, input position): by nondecreasing weight, with edges of equal weight in input order.

results.title: Discrete parent forest
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The initial forest on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is the parent forest in which every vertex is its own parent, so every vertex is a root, and whose depth certificate is $0$ at every vertex.

results.title: Connectivity by a newest-first edge list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Connectivity of vertices $u$ and $v$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ by a list of validated edges, read newest first, is defined by recursion on the list. By the empty list, $u$ and $v$ are connected exactly when $u = v$. results.title: Connectivity by an edge list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Vertices $u$ and $v$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ are connected by a list $e_1, \dots, e_k$ of validated edges when they are connected by the reversed list $e_k, \dots, e_1$ in the sense of connectivity by a newest-first edge list.

results.title: Acyclicity of a newest-first edge list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A list $e_1, \dots, e_k$ of validated edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, read newest first, is newest-first acyclic when, for every $i$, the endpoints of $e_i$ are not connected by the later list $e_{i+1}, \dots, e_k$ in the sense of connectivity by a newest-first edge list.

results.title: Acyclic edge list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A list $e_1, \dots, e_k$ of validated edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is acyclic when, for every $i$, the endpoints of $e_i$ are not connected by the preceding edges $e_1, \dots, e_{i-1}$, in the sense of connectivity by an edge list.

results.title: Edge lists spanning a graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A list $L$ of validated edges spans a finite weighted multigraph $G$ on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ when, for every valid input edge of $G$ (one whose endpoints are both less than $n$), the two endpoints of that edge are connected using the edges of $L$.

results.title: Spanning forest of an input graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an input graph $G$ on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, a list $F$ of validated edges is a spanning forest of $G$ when every edge of $F$ is a valid edge of $G$, $F$ is acyclic, and $F$ spans $G$: for every valid edge of $G$, its endpoints are connected by $F$.

results.title: Ordered spanning forest
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an input graph $G$ on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, a list $e_1, \dots, e_k$ of validated edges is an ordered spanning forest of $G$ when it is a spanning forest of $G$ and its keys are nondecreasing: for all $i < j$, the key of $e_i$ is at most the key of $e_j$, where the key of an edge with weight $w$ and input ordinal $o$ is the pair $(w, o)$ and keys are compared lexicographically.

results.title: Total weight of a Kruskal edge list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The total weight of a list of validated edges is the sum of the weights of its entries, each entry counted once, so parallel edges and repeated entries each contribute their weight.

results.title: Kruskal scan state
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A state of the Kruskal scan on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ consists of a union-find parent forest on these vertices, which records the current partition, and the list of edges accepted so far, newest first.

results.title: One Kruskal step
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $s$ be a Kruskal scan state and $e$ a validated edge with endpoints $u$ and $v$. If $u$ and $v$ are equivalent in the union-find forest of $s$, processing $e$ leaves $s$ unchanged. Otherwise $e$ is accepted: the new forest is the union of $u$ and $v$ in the forest of $s$, and $e$ is put at the front of the list of accepted edges.

results.title: Scanning a list of edges
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Starting from a Kruskal scan state $s$, scanning a list of validated edges $e_1, \dots, e_k$ applies one Kruskal step to each edge in list order: the scan of the empty list returns $s$, and the scan of $e_1, \dots, e_k$ is the scan of $e_2, \dots, e_k$ from the state obtained by processing $e_1$ in $s$.

results.title: Kruskal selects only valid input edges
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, every edge in the list returned by Kruskal's algorithm on $G$ is a valid edge of $G$: an input edge whose two endpoints are both below $n$, carrying its input ordinal.

results.title: Kruskal's output is acyclic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every graph $G$, the edge list returned by Kruskal's algorithm on $G$ is acyclic: each edge in it joins two vertices that are not connected by the edges before it in the list.

results.title: Kruskal's selected edges span the graph

results.title: Kruskal's output is a spanning forest
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every graph $G$, the edge list returned by Kruskal's algorithm on $G$ is a spanning forest of $G$: every edge in it is a valid edge of $G$, it is acyclic, and it connects the two endpoints of every valid edge of $G$.

results.title: Kruskal's output is a sorted spanning forest
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every graph $G$, the edge list returned by Kruskal's algorithm on $G$ is a spanning forest of $G$ (its edges are valid edges of $G$, it is acyclic, and it connects the endpoints of every valid edge of $G$), and whenever an edge $e$ comes before an edge $f$ in it, the key (weight, input ordinal) of $e$ is lexicographically at most that of $f$.

results.title: Kruskal's algorithm gives a minimum spanning forest
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a graph with natural-number edge weights, and let $F$ be any spanning forest of $G$: a list of valid edges of $G$ that is acyclic and connects the endpoints of every valid edge of $G$. Then the total weight of the edge list returned by Kruskal's algorithm on $G$ is at most the total weight of $F$.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given an interpretation $I$ assigning a type $I(b)$ to each base type $b$, the denotation $[\![A]\!]_I$ of a simple type $A$ is defined by recursion on $A$: a base type $b$ denotes $I(b)$, and a function type $A \Rightarrow B$ denotes the type of all functions from $[\![A]\!]_I$ to $[\![B]\!]_I$.

results.title: Semantic environments for the denotational semantics of STLC
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Given an interpretation $I$ assigning a type to each base type and a typing context $\Gamma$ (a list of simple types), an environment for $\Gamma$ assigns to every variable $x$ of $\Gamma$, of any simple type $A$, an element of the denotation $[\![A]\!]_I$.

results.title: Extending a semantic environment in STLC
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given an interpretation $I$ of the base types, a value $a$ in the denotation of a type $A$ and an environment $\eta$ for a context $\Gamma$, the extended environment for the context $A :: \Gamma$ sends the newest variable to $a$ and the successor $\mathrm{succ}\,x$ of each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\eta(x)$.

results.title: Renaming an environment
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a renaming $\rho$ from context $\Gamma$ to context $\Delta$ (a type-preserving map from the variables of $\Gamma$ to those of $\Delta$) and an environment $\eta$ for $\Delta$, the renamed environment for $\Gamma$ sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\eta(\rho(x))$; that is, it is the composite $\eta \circ \rho$.

results.title: Denotation of an STLC term
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given an interpretation $I$ of the base types, the denotation of a well-typed term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ in an environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$ is the element of the denotation of $A$ defined by recursion on $t$: a variable $x$ denotes $\eta(x)$, an application $f\,a$ denotes the denotation of $f$ applied to the denotation of $a$ (both in $\eta$), and an abstraction $\lambda.\,b$ denotes the function…

results.title: Renaming lemma for STLC denotation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every type-preserving renaming $\rho$ from context $\Gamma$ to context $\Delta$, every term $t$ in context $\Gamma$ and every environment $\eta$ for $\Delta$, the denotation in $\eta$ of the term obtained by renaming the variables of $t$ along $\rho$ equals the denotation of $t$ in the environment that sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\eta(\rho(x))$.

results.title: Weakening preserves STLC denotation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, every type $B$, every value $a$ in the denotation of $B$ and every environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$, the weakening of $t$ to the context $B :: \Gamma$ has, in the environment that extends $\eta$ by $a$ for the newest variable, the same denotation as $t$ in $\eta$.

results.title: Denotation of an STLC substitution
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given an interpretation $I$ of the base types, a type-preserving substitution $\sigma$ mapping each variable of a context $\Gamma$ to a term in a context $\Delta$, and an environment $\eta$ for $\Delta$, this is the environment for $\Gamma$ that sends each variable $x$ to the denotation of $\sigma(x)$ in $\eta$.

results.title: Substitution lemma for STLC denotation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every type-preserving substitution $\sigma$ mapping each variable of a context $\Gamma$ to a term in a context $\Delta$, every term $t$ in context $\Gamma$ and every environment $\eta$ for $\Delta$, the denotation in $\eta$ of $t$ with $\sigma$ applied simultaneously to its variables equals the denotation of $t$ in the environment that sends each variable $x$ of…

results.title: Denotation of an instantiated STLC body
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every term $b$ of type $B$ in context $A :: \Gamma$, every term $a$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ and every environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$, the denotation in $\eta$ of $b$ with its newest variable replaced by $a$ equals the denotation of $b$ in the environment that extends $\eta$ by the denotation of $a$ in $\eta$ for the newest variable.

results.title: One reduction step preserves STLC denotation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, if a term $t$ reduces to $t'$ in one step of call-by-value reduction, then $t$ and $t'$ have the same denotation in every environment $\eta$ for their context.

results.title: Multi-step reduction preserves STLC denotation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, if a term $t$ reduces to $t'$ in zero or more steps of call-by-value reduction, then $t$ and $t'$ have the same denotation in every environment $\eta$ for their context.

results.title: Big-step evaluation preserves STLC denotation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, if a term $t$ evaluates to $v$ under call-by-value big-step evaluation, then $t$ and $v$ have the same denotation in every environment $\eta$ for their context.

results.title: Semantic equality of terms in a model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types as types. Two terms $t$ and $u$ of the same type $A$ in the same context $\Gamma$ are semantically equal in $I$ when, for every semantic environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$, the denotation of $t$ in $I$ at $\eta$ equals the denotation of $u$ in $I$ at $\eta$.

results.title: Semantic equality is reflexive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every term $t$ is semantically equal to itself in $I$: it has the same denotation as itself in every environment.

results.title: Symmetry of semantic equality of terms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types and all terms $t$ and $u$ of the same type in the same context, if $t$ and $u$ are semantically equal in $I$, then $u$ and $t$ are semantically equal in $I$.

results.title: Transitivity of semantic equality of terms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types and all terms $t$, $u$ and $w$ of the same type in the same context, if $t$ and $u$ are semantically equal in $I$ and $u$ and $w$ are semantically equal in $I$, then $t$ and $w$ are semantically equal in $I$.

results.title: Semantic equality is a congruence for application
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types. If terms $f$ and $g$ of type $A \Rightarrow B$ in a context $\Gamma$ are semantically equal in $I$ (they have the same denotation in every environment), and terms $a$ and $b$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ are semantically equal in $I$, then the applications $f\,a$ and $g\,b$ are semantically equal in $I$.

results.title: Semantic equality is a congruence for lambda abstraction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types. If two terms of type $B$ in the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$ are semantically equal in $I$ (they have the same denotation in every environment), then their lambda abstractions, terms of type $A \Rightarrow B$ in $\Gamma$, are semantically equal in $I$.

results.title: Renaming preserves semantic equality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types. If terms $t$ and $u$ of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ are semantically equal in $I$ (they have the same denotation in every environment), then for every type-preserving renaming $\rho$ of the variables of $\Gamma$ into a context $\Delta$, the renamed terms $\rho(t)$ and $\rho(u)$ are semantically equal in $I$.

results.title: Substitution preserves semantic equality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, if two terms $t$ and $u$ of the same type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ are semantically equal in $I$, then for every simultaneous substitution $\sigma$ from $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, the result of applying $\sigma$ to $t$ and the result of applying $\sigma$ to $u$ are semantically equal in $I$.

results.title: Single-step evaluation is a semantic equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, if a term $t$ reduces to a term $u$ in one call-by-value evaluation step, then $t$ and $u$ are semantically equal in $I$: they have the same denotation in every environment.

results.title: Multi-step evaluation is a semantic equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, if a term $t$ reduces to a term $u$ in zero or more call-by-value evaluation steps, then $t$ and $u$ are semantically equal in $I$: they have the same denotation in every environment.

results.title: Beta is sound for the denotational semantics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every term $t$ of type $B$ in the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, and every term $a$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, the redex $(\lambda.\,t)\,a$ is semantically equal in $I$ (has the same denotation in every environment) to the instantiation $t[a]$, which replaces the newest free variable of $t$ by $a$.

results.title: Eta is sound for the denotational semantics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types and every term $f$ of type $A \Rightarrow B$ in a context $\Gamma$, let $f'$ be the weakening of $f$ to the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable $x$ of type $A$. Then the term $\lambda x.\, f'\,x$, which binds $x$, is semantically equal to $f$ in $I$ (has the same denotation in every environment).

results.title: Pointwise semantic equality of substitutions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types as types. Two simultaneous substitutions $\sigma$ and $\tau$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$ are pointwise semantically equal in $I$ when, for every variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ (of any type) and every semantic environment $\eta$ for $\Delta$, the denotation of the term $\sigma(x)$ in $I$ at $\eta$ equals the denotation of the term $\tau(x)$ in $I$ at $\eta$.

results.title: Pointwise semantic equality of substitutions is reflexive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types and every simultaneous substitution $\sigma$ that replaces each variable of a context $\Gamma$ by a term of the same type in a context $\Delta$, $\sigma$ is pointwise semantically equal to itself in $I$: for every variable $x$ of $\Gamma$, the term $\sigma(x)$ has the same denotation as itself in every environment for $\Delta$.

results.title: Symmetry of pointwise semantic equality of substitutions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types and all simultaneous substitutions $\sigma$ and $\tau$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, if $\sigma$ and $\tau$ are pointwise semantically equal in $I$, then $\tau$ and $\sigma$ are pointwise semantically equal in $I$.

results.title: Transitivity of pointwise semantic equality of substitutions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types and all simultaneous substitutions $\sigma$, $\tau$ and $\upsilon$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, if $\sigma$ and $\tau$ are pointwise semantically equal in $I$ and $\tau$ and $\upsilon$ are pointwise semantically equal in $I$, then $\sigma$ and $\upsilon$ are pointwise semantically equal in $I$.

results.title: Semantically equal substitutions give semantically equal results
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every term $t$ of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$, and all simultaneous substitutions $\sigma$ and $\tau$ from $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$ that are pointwise semantically equal in $I$, the result of applying $\sigma$ to $t$ and the result of applying $\tau$ to $t$ are semantically equal in $I$.

results.title: Semantic equality is an equivalence relation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every context $\Gamma$ and every type $A$, semantic equality in $I$ of terms of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ (having the same denotation in every environment) is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

results.title: Plugging a term into an STLC context
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E$ be a typed one-hole context whose hole has type $A$ in variable context $\Gamma$ and which produces a term of type $B$ in variable context $\Delta$. For a term $t$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, the plugged term $E[t]$ of type $B$ in $\Delta$ is defined by recursion on $E$: $[\,][t] = t$, $(E\,a)[t] = E[t]\,a$, $(f\,E)[t] = f\,E[t]$ and $(\lambda.\,E)[t] = \lambda.\,E[t]$, where $[\,]$ is the bare hole, $E\,a$…

results.title: Composition of STLC contexts
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E_2$ be a typed one-hole context whose hole has type $B$ in variable context $\Delta$ and which produces a term of type $C$ in context $\Theta$, and let $E_1$ be one whose hole has type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ and which produces a term of type $B$ in $\Delta$. The composite $E_2 \circ E_1$, with hole of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ and result of type $C$ in $\Theta$, replaces the hole of $E_2$ by $E_1$; by recursion…

results.title: Plugging into a composite STLC context
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E_2$ be a typed one-hole context whose hole has type $B$ in variable context $\Delta$ and which produces a term of type $C$ in context $\Theta$, and let $E_1$ be one whose hole has type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ and which produces a term of type $B$ in $\Delta$. Then for every term $t$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, $(E_2 \circ E_1)[t] = E_2[E_1[t]]$.

results.title: Associativity of composition of STLC contexts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E_1$ be a typed one-hole context whose hole has type $A$ in variable context $\Gamma$ and which produces a term of type $B$ in context $\Delta$, $E_2$ one with hole of type $B$ in $\Delta$ producing type $C$ in $\Theta$, and $E_3$ one with hole of type $C$ in $\Theta$ producing type $D$ in $\Xi$. Then $(E_3 \circ E_2) \circ E_1 = E_3 \circ (E_2 \circ E_1)$.

results.title: Semantic equality is a congruence for typed contexts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types. Let $t$ and $u$ be terms of type $A$ in variable context $\Gamma$ that denote the same value in $I$ under every semantic environment. Then for every typed one-hole context $C$ whose hole has type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ and which produces a term of type $B$ in context $\Delta$, the terms $C[t]$ and $C[u]$ obtained by plugging $t$ and $u$ into the hole also denote the…

results.title: Model equality of STLC terms
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two terms $t$ and $u$ of type $A$ in variable context $\Gamma$ are model-equal when, for every interpretation $I$ of the base types by types in the same universe as the type of base types, they are semantically equal in $I$: with function types interpreted as full function spaces, the denotations of $t$ and $u$ agree at every semantic environment for $\Gamma$.

results.title: Model equality is a congruence for STLC contexts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a typed one-hole context whose hole has type $A$ in variable context $\Gamma$ and which produces a term of type $B$ in context $\Delta$. If two terms $t$ and $u$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ are model-equal, then $E[t]$ and $E[u]$ are model-equal.

results.title: Model-independent beta equality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every term $b$ of type $B$ in the variable context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, and every term $a$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, the application $(\lambda.\,b)\,a$ is model-equal to $b[a]$, the result of substituting $a$ for the newest variable of $b$.

results.title: Model-independent eta equality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every term $f$ of type $A \Rightarrow B$ in variable context $\Gamma$, the term $\lambda.\,(f^{\uparrow}\,x_0)$ is model-equal to $f$, where $f^{\uparrow}$ is $f$ weakened by a newest variable of type $A$ and $x_0$ is that variable.

results.title: Beta equality inside an STLC context
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a typed one-hole context whose hole has type $B$ in variable context $\Gamma$ and which produces a term of type $C$ in context $\Delta$. For every term $b$ of type $B$ in $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, and every term $a$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, the term $E[(\lambda.\,b)\,a]$ is model-equal to $E[b[a]]$, where $b[a]$ is the result of substituting $a$ for the newest variable of $b$.

results.title: Eta equality inside an STLC context
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a typed one-hole context whose hole has type $A \Rightarrow B$ in variable context $\Gamma$ and which produces a term of type $C$ in context $\Delta$. For every term $f$ of type $A \Rightarrow B$ in $\Gamma$, the term $E[\lambda.\,(f^{\uparrow}\,x_0)]$ is model-equal to $E[f]$, where $f^{\uparrow}$ is $f$ weakened by a newest variable of type $A$ and $x_0$ is that variable.
